p.title: Tenali and the boastful merchant
p.challenge: Put the witty tale in order: challenge, clever reply, surprising ending

panels.t: A proud merchant boasts, "I can sell anything, even air!"
Tenali hands him an empty jar of "fresh Vijayanagara breeze".
"Sell me this jar for one gold coin," says Tenali.
The merchant peeps in: "But it is empty!"
"Exactly, and so was your boast." The whole court laughs, even the merchant.

p.title: Fact, inference or guess?
p.challenge: Think like a detective: can it be checked (fact), does a clue support it (inference), or is there no clue at all (guess)? Then press Check.

items.text: Her umbrella is dripping on the floor.
items.why: You can look and check it directly: a fact.

items.text: The clock in the hall shows 4 o'clock.
items.why: Anyone can check the clock: a fact.

items.text: Umbrella dripping, so it was raining.
items.why: A sensible conclusion from a clue (the wet umbrella): an inference.

items.text: He keeps yawning, so he is sleepy.
items.why: The yawning is a clue that supports it: an inference.

items.text: Muddy shoes, so he walked through mud.
items.why: The muddy shoes are the clue: an inference.

items.text: The new boy's favourite colour is blue.
items.why: No clue supports it: a guess.

items.text: The visitor is probably a famous singer.
items.why: Nothing in the scene points to it: a guess.

p.title: Bibha Chowdhuri's journey
